name: OYATSUYA 323（おやつや みつみ） (OYATSUYA 323 (Oyatsuya Mitsumi))

claims.text: Everything sold is wheat-flour baked goods made in the same small kitchen, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable throughout the shop.
Items are made with butter, eggs and dairy; no separation from animal products is documented.
Hamburger steak is a core dish and typically contains wheat-based binders; sauces are onion/red-wine based with no stated gluten-free preparation.
Entirely a beef/pork teppan concept (hamburger and steak); no vegan or vegetarian dishes are documented.

name: ピーワイハラールキッチン (PY Halal Kitchen)

claims.text: Menu centers on naan, roti and noodle/udon dishes that contain wheat; no gluten-free preparation or separation is documented.
Primarily a meat-based halal kitchen (chicken, lamb, beef); vegetarian dishes may share equipment and often include dairy or egg, so vegan separation is not assured.
Fully halal kitchen with no alcohol and no pork, run by a Muslim owner; vegetarian options are available for diners who avoid meat.
Photo-illustrated menus make it easier to identify dish contents and ask about ingredients.
The signature chickpea curry and the seasonal lunch are centered on legumes, vegetables and whole grains, so plant-based diners have substantial options.
Sukiyaki and shabu-shabu are prepared with soy-sauce-based broth/dipping sauces, which in Japan are standardly brewed with wheat; no wheat-free alternative is documented.

name: リストランテ ボルゴ・コニシ (Ristorante Borgo Konishi)

claims.text: The kitchen is a pasta-trained, bread-and-pasta-forward Italian operation, so gluten is heavily present and cross-contamination should be assumed; no gluten-free protocol is documented.
Courses rely on typical Italian animal products (cheese, butter, stocks) and local fish/meat; no separate vegan preparation is documented.
The restaurant is fully reservation-only and serves bespoke courses, so allergies and dietary needs would normally be raised at booking, but no specific allergy-handling policy is published.

name: ロッカン ルーム（ROKKAN ROOM） (ROKKAN ROOM)

claims.text: Signature nyūmen uses Miwa sōmen (wheat noodles) and the menu includes curries, so wheat is central to the kitchen; no gluten-free preparation or separation is documented.
Nyūmen broth is typically fish-based and the custard pudding uses eggs; no vegan menu or animal-free assurances were found.
As a traditional kaiseki ryotei, dishes rely on soy sauce, miso, and dashi; no gluten-free or wheat-free menu is documented, so wheat-derived seasonings should be assumed present.
Courses center on seasonal seafood (including whole sea bream) and likely fish/kombu dashi, so standard menus are not vegan and shared kitchen prep is expected.
The restaurant asks that allergy and dietary restrictions be communicated at least 3 business days in advance.
Menus are made to order each day by the head chef, which means dietary requests arranged well ahead may be accommodated.
